subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK/function-calling fit
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>, Tom Li <tom.li@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 14:00:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: Redwood integration & SDK/function-calling fit

Hi Jenna / Tom —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our call and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Top pain points you confirmed:
- End-user latency spikes during peak traffic (notably on long context threads).
- Cost per 1k queries is higher than expected due to low batching across your existing endpoint config.
- Need for deterministic output structure (JSON-like) for downstream ingestion into your search/reranking pipeline.

Goals you shared:
1) Reduce median latency for chat flows under 300ms for short queries and keep tail latency under SLA.
2) Enable structured outputs and function calling so your assistants can surface exact fields to the product feed.
3) Use embeddings + reranking to improve relevance for your internal search (goal: +8–12% lift in NDCG).

Product/integ fit notes we discussed:
- SDK changes: we recommend embedding our new streaming SDK (node/python) which supports incremental token streaming + function-calling hooks. This will let you render partial responses in the UI while the final structured payload is assembled.
- Function calling: Redwood has native function calling support and can return structured JSON for downstream consumers. We discussed the two integration patterns: in-process validation (SDK parses/validates JSON) vs. server-side validation (Redwood returns JSON string, then your backend validates). We recommend server-side validation to start to avoid client-side parsing issues.
- Streaming & structured outputs: streaming reduces perceived latency; function-calling + schema enforcement gets you predictable outputs for the product feed.
- Embeddings & reranking: suggest a small pilot using our 768-d Open-embedding model with a 50k-item index to validate NDCG improvements. We can provide sample scripts to compute embeddings and test rerank latency.

Immediate next steps (owner / ETA):
- Marissa: send integration guide + sample streaming SDK snippets (attached) — by EOD today.
- Tom: share a representative dataset (10–20 queries + expected structured output) and a point-of-contact for infra (SRE) — by 2027-03-25.
- Vivek: coordinate an internal deep-dive with your SRE and data-engineering teams to scope Dedicated capacity if needed — propose dates next week.

Attachments: redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (SDK examples + function-calling snippets), acme-inference-requirements.xlsx (we asked Tom for the dataset template).

If I missed anything or you want items reordered, let me know — otherwise I’ll follow up with the sample code and a proposed pilot plan.

Best,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Thanks Jenna — great questions. Short answers here and attached pointers: 

- Schema enforcement: Redwood can enforce output schemas via function-calling + post-generation validators in the serving runtime. For strict production enforcement we typically add a lightweight server-side validation step (we include sample validation code in the attachment). If you want strict model-level blocking (reject responses that don't match), we can enable a validation hook but recommend staged rollout.
- Reranking latency: for the pilot we recommend Redwood-hosted test infra to isolate variables; that will give us clean latency numbers. If results look good we'll run a side-by-side on your staging infra. Pilot targets: aim for <200ms P95 for rerank with a 50k candidate index using our batched embedding + ANN retrieval.
- HubSpot/DocuSign: attaching a sample SOW template and sharing HubSpot opportunity link in metadata. If the legal/ procurement team wants different wording, we can iterate quickly.

Next concrete items I’ll send today:
1) redwood-sdk-integration-guide.pdf (attached) — includes streaming SDK snippets, function-calling examples, and server-side validation snippet.
2) small pilot proposal (1–2 week eval) with success metrics and optional Dedicated capacity sizing.

Could we lock a 45-minute SRE sync on Thurs 2027-03-25 at 10:00am PT? Vivek — can you propose a calendar invite?

Cheers,
Marissa
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
